series.title: 20th Century Boys
series.note: The 22 volumes are followed by a two-volume conclusion, 21st Century Boys, not counted here. VIZ Media also released a Perfect Edition that combines volumes.

series.title: Attack on Titan
series.note: Kodansha publishes the English edition. Its larger Colossal Editions collect several volumes each, so count them separately from single volumes.

series.title: Berserk
series.note: Dark Horse publishes the English edition, and most of its Deluxe hardcovers collect three volumes. The series continued after Kentaro Miura’s death in 2021, under Kouji Mori and Studio Gaga.

series.title: Black Clover
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which follows the original volume numbering.

series.title: Bleach
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition. It also released 3-in-1 omnibuses, so check which format you are buying before you fill a gap.

series.title: Blue Lock
series.note: Kodansha publishes the English edition. The spin-off Blue Lock: Episode Nagi has separate numbering and is not part of this checklist.

series.title: Chainsaw Man
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition. Part 1 ends at volume 11, and Part 2 continues the same numbering from volume 12.

series.title: Dandadan
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which usually trails the Japanese release by a few volumes.

series.title: Death Note
series.note: The story runs 12 volumes. VIZ Media also published a guidebook, How to Read, plus Black Edition and All-in-One versions, so a shelf can look quite different depending on format.

series.title: Delicious in Dungeon
series.note: Published in Japanese as Dungeon Meshi. Yen Press publishes the English edition.

series.title: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, and a complete box set exists if you would rather buy the series in one go.

series.title: Dragon Ball
series.note: The 42 Japanese volumes are split in VIZ Media’s English release into Dragon Ball (16 volumes) and Dragon Ball Z (26 volumes), so English numbering restarts partway through.

series.title: Fairy Tail
series.note: Kodansha publishes the English edition. The sequel, Fairy Tail: 100 Years Quest, has its own numbering and is not counted here.

series.title: Fire Force
series.note: Kodansha publishes the English edition. Its single volumes follow the original numbering, and it also sells 3-in-1 omnibuses with their own numbering.

series.title: Frieren: Beyond Journey’s End
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition. The original run takes occasional serialization breaks, so new volumes can be irregular.

series.title: Fruits Basket
series.note: The original English run of 23 volumes came from Tokyopop. Yen Press later released a Collector’s Edition of 12 larger books.

series.title: Fullmetal Alchemist
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, along with 3-in-1 omnibuses and larger Fullmetal Edition hardcovers.

series.title: Golden Kamuy
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which follows the original volume numbering.

series.title: Goodnight Punpun
series.note: The 13 Japanese volumes are collected in English by VIZ Media as seven larger books, so your English shelf will look much shorter than this list.

series.title: Haikyu!!
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which follows the original volume numbering.

series.title: Horimiya
series.note: Adapted from Hero’s webcomic Hori-san to Miyamura-kun. Yen Press publishes the English edition.

series.title: Hunter x Hunter
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition. The series has a long history of publication breaks, so long gaps between new volumes are normal.

series.title: Jujutsu Kaisen
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition. The prequel, Jujutsu Kaisen 0, is a separate book outside the main numbering, so this checklist does not include it.

series.title: Kaguya-sama: Love Is War
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which follows the original volume numbering.

series.title: Kaiju No. 8
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which follows the original volume numbering.

series.title: Mob Psycho 100
series.note: Dark Horse publishes the English edition.

series.title: Monster
series.note: VIZ Media published the 18 original volumes in English and later The Perfect Edition, nine larger books that combine them.

series.title: My Hero Academia
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition. Spin-offs like Vigilantes have their own numbering and are not part of this checklist.

series.title: Naruto
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, along with 3-in-1 omnibuses that are often a cheaper way to fill gaps.

series.title: One Piece
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, and also sells 3-in-1 omnibus editions and box sets that cover the same story with different numbering.

series.title: One-Punch Man
series.note: Yusuke Murata’s redrawn version of ONE’s webcomic. VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which trails the Japanese release.

series.title: Oshi no Ko
series.note: Yen Press publishes the English edition, which follows the original volume numbering.

series.title: Sakamoto Days
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which usually trails the Japanese release by a few volumes.

series.title: Slam Dunk
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the 31-volume English edition.

series.title: Spy x Family
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition, which usually trails the Japanese release by a few volumes.

series.title: Tokyo Ghoul
series.note: VIZ Media publishes the English edition. The sequel, Tokyo Ghoul:re, has its own 16 volumes and is not counted here.

series.title: Tokyo Revengers
series.note: In English, Seven Seas publishes the print edition as omnibuses that combine two volumes, so the English book count is lower than the Japanese one.

series.title: Vinland Saga
series.note: Kodansha’s English hardcovers combine two Japanese volumes in most books, so an English shelf has far fewer books than the Japanese count.
